prior_importants.description: The suffix expansion also runs on commit-SHA permalinks, so a SHA link now fires adr-area or module-boundary where the same bare path does not. The ref-is-one-segment behavior regresses for GitHub's default permalink form.

findings.description: The dot-segment guard `!segments[length - 1]?.startsWith('.')` only looks at the last segment of each candidate ref. A longer ref that still contains a dot segment gets through. For `https://github.com/acme/tool/blob/main/.template/app/src/claude/hooks.ts` with ADR area `src/claude/**`, the ref `main/.template` is dropped, but `main/.template/app` is accepted. That gives the candidate `src/claude/hooks.ts`, so adr-area fires even though the real path is outside the area. The new test only passes because the wrongly accepted candidate there, `README.md`, misses `.claude/**`. Fix: check every ref segment, `segments.slice(0, length).every((segment) => !segment.startsWith('.'))`.

`SHA_REF` (`/^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/i`) reads any first segment of 7 or more hex or digit characters as a SHA, so only ref length 1 is tried. A date-named slash branch such as `https://github.com/acme/tool/blob/20241123/hotfix/src/claude/hooks.ts` with ADR area `src/claude/**` now gives only `hotfix/src/claude/hooks.ts` and no longer fires adr-area. The previous commit fired here, and missing it is a false negative, against the PR's 'err toward firing'. Fix: take the SHA shortcut only when the segment holds a letter, or is the full 40 characters.

The `MAX_REF_SEGMENTS` JSDoc says "The most slashes a permalink's ref is read as holding", but the constant counts segments. Ref lengths 1 to 4 means at most 4 segments, which is 3 slashes. Someone tuning the cap or writing a boundary test from the comment would be off by one. Suggested wording: "The most segments a permalink's ref is read as holding; real refs hold few, and it bounds the candidates."

`refLengths` is a nested ternary whose literal `[1]` SHA branch repeats what the `Array.from(...).filter(...)` branch computes with a cap of 1, so a reader has to check the two agree. Using the SHA test only to pick the cap (`const cap = SHA_REF.test(segments[0] ?? '') ? 1 : MAX_REF_SEGMENTS;`) leaves one way to generate candidates. It also stops a bare SHA link with no path, such as `blob/3d35d70`, from producing an empty-string candidate.

process_issues.description: Skipped by gate: review-context (no spec, protocol or infra surface), review-workflow-safety (no .github/workflows change), review-spec (no spec source: the PR closes no issue), review-maintainability (not on the default roster). No validator ran because no important finding survived.
